_comment: The week in the C Cubed. The scheduled job appends one object to weeks[] after each week finalizes: a lede, a write-up for each of the six games, and an 'around' notebook covering everything else that moved that week. articles[] holds longer pieces — the Tuesday recap column, midweek previews, odds and big-trade pieces, the Saturday odds column, draft reports — written by the routines in ROUTINES.md or by hand. Every article carries a plain-text teaser ending in its own #news/<slug> link. A routine appends its one article and carries every existing one through untouched. The site sorts both newest-first and computes risers and sliders itself from its own power rankings, so nothing here should ever quote a rank or a movement.

articles.headline: Nobody wanted a quarterback, and Josh Jacobs paid for it
articles.dek: Six backs, six receivers, two tight ends at the turn — and a top-32 running back still sitting there at pick 101.

cover.caption: The first four off the board: Gibbs, Robinson, Chase, Nacua.

blocks.text: The first draft this league has ever held ran on Sunday evening and took seventy-nine minutes end to end — fifteen rounds, a hundred and eighty picks, not one traded slot, and an average of twenty-seven seconds between names. For eight picks it went exactly the way the market said it would. Then it stopped doing that, and it never really started again.
the average gap between picks. A hundred and eighty of them, start to finish, in an hour and twenty minutes.
Six backs, six receivers, nothing else

The first round split exactly down the middle and touched no other position — no quarterback, no tight end, no thought given to either. It was also the most obedient stretch of the night: none of the first eight picks moved more than two places off its pre-draft price. jiddyyyyyy opened with Jahmyr Gibbs from the one slot, yojarshh took Bijan Robinson behind him, and the receivers came in the order the board had them.

The turn is where it loosened. drewkim took James Cook at 9 and andychoe03 took Chase Brown at 10, both roughly three picks ahead of the board, and from the back of the round nikhil1123 got Justin Jefferson at 12 and De'Von Achane at 13 — the only manager to leave the first two rounds with a receiver and a back both priced inside the top thirteen.
Two tight ends, then twenty picks of silence

edyun1 broke the position at 21 with Brock Bowers, fourteen picks ahead of the market, and Lee284 followed immediately with Trey McBride, seven ahead of his. Both of them play in tech, and having taken the two best tight ends off the board they then watched twenty picks go by before anyone else touched the position — Tyler Warren, to jjnhwg, at 42.
Thirty-three picks of everybody waiting for somebody else

Josh Allen went to andychoe03 at 34, and he was the first quarterback drafted. The twelfth team to take one was yojarshh, at pick 122. That is a room in which nobody wanted to be first, and the market punished the position all the way down: four starters with real prices sat there until somebody finally took pity.
Josh Jacobs, pick 101
picks past his price. Jacobs came off the pre-draft board at 31.4 and sat until saiky7 took him at 101 — the longest fall of the night by eight picks.

Nothing complicated happened to him. blocks.text: Twelve teams, three divisions of four, fourteen weeks and six playoff places. The three division winners take the first three seeds whatever their records look like, and the two best of those get the bye. Everything below is a projection off the draft and nothing else — nobody has played a game — but the shape of the season is already fixed, and the shape says the divisions matter more than the rosters do.
of every team's games are inside its own division. You play each of your three rivals twice and everybody else once — checked against the schedule Sleeper has actually posted, not assumed.
The best of the draft, and the widest gap in it

yojarshh came out of the draft with the most valuable roster in the league — Bijan Robinson, Pickens, Rice, Adams — and he is the shortest price on the board to win the whole thing at +700. Behind him saiky7 holds the Josh Jacobs steal and a Jaxon Smith-Njigba–Drake London receiving pair, nikhil1123 has Jefferson and Achane from the back of round one, and jjnhwg has Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry and the least help behind them. As a group it drafted better than either of the others; it is also the division where the favourite is furthest clear of the field.
Three teams inside a point and a half

Lee284, jiddyyyyyy and edyun1 came out of the draft separated by 1.5 points a week — which, over fourteen games against a weekly swing of twenty-four points, is not a separation at all. The board prices them +230, +260 and +270 to win the division — forty points covering three teams, where no other division gets its top three inside a hundred — and the only reason it is a market at all is tonypng at +390. Two of these three teams also own the best tight ends in the league, taken back to back at 21 and 22, which is either the reason they are level or a coincidence that will look like a reason by November.
The worst division, and the cheapest bye in the league

On drafted value cville is the weakest of the three — 106.1 a week on average against chaps' 108.9 — and it holds the longest title price on the board in drewkim at +1500, with asierbelay at +1330 not far above him. bigmoneyjos is the favourite at +210 on the back of McCaffrey, A.J. Brown and Nico Collins, with andychoe03 and the only Josh Allen in the league behind him.

None of which stops one of these four from being seeded first or second in January. That is the format working as designed: win the softest division and you are a top-three seed regardless of what the other eight teams did. It shows up in the numbers as a wash — cville's four teams share 61.9% of a bye between them against chaps' 70.5%, a gap far smaller than the gap between the rosters.

blocks.text: Nobody is a lock and nobody is out of it

Six of twelve teams make the playoffs, so the average team is a coin flip by definition. What is striking is how little the draft moved anyone off that coin flip: the best team in the league is projected to make it 60.4% of the time and the worst 41.4%, and every other team sits between them.

separate the best playoff odds in the league from the worst. Across fourteen games, that is the difference between 7.5 projected wins and 6.6 — the best draft in the league bought about nine-tenths of a win.

The win totals say the same thing in plainer language. Six teams are priced at seven and a half wins and six at six and a half, and not one projects above 7.5. There is no team here that has to be beaten and no team here that can be written off, which is the most anyone can honestly say about a league that has never played a down.

blocks.text: Week 6 was the lowest-scoring week of C Cubed's first season — 1,353.14 points across six games, 311.58 fewer than week 5 — and the six teams that lost left 233.02 points on their benches, against 78.90 for the six that won. Tshough (tonypng) scored 168.86, the only score of the week above 136, and beat Uzzz uzz uzz (jjnhwg) by 87.56. 8 and thick (bigmoneyjos) won for the first time, so no team is winless.
Points left on the bench by the six losing teams in week 6. The six winning teams left 78.90 between them.
Winners Kept Their Best Players in the Lineup

Bench points are scored by players a manager did not start, and the split by result is lopsided. Of the 78.90 the winners left, n² (nikhil1123) accounted for none and tonypng for 3, from the Seattle defense. The two winners with the most unused, bigmoneyjos at 28.10 and Lucky Strike (drewkim) at 24.70, won anyway, by 17 and 34.3.

A bench total overstates what a lineup change could have captured, because only a player at the right position can take a slot. The better test is one player against the starter he would replace, and by that test the three losing benches that outscored their margin tell three different stories.
Three Losses Where the Bench Outscored the Margin

Jug (Lee284) left 61.44 points on the bench, the most of any team, and lost by 12.14. S2? #jtw #imwallin (yojarshh) left 37.88 and lost by 6.08. BOWSER (edyun1) left 45.40 and lost by 34.30. Lee284's case is the nearest to a swap. Trevor Lawrence scored 28.34 on the bench while Brock Purdy scored 17.36 in the quarterback slot, a 10.98-point difference in a game lost by 12.14. The one-for-one swap leaves Lee284 1.16 short.

The Lowest-Scoring Week Still Had a Blowout

Week 6 averaged 112.76 points a team. Week 2, the next lowest, averaged 123.78 (1,485.32 across the six games), and week 5 averaged 138.73 (1,664.72). Three teams scored under 100: andychoe03 at 93.84, jjnhwg at 81.30 and edyun1 at 78.98.

blocks.text: Week 7 set the season's scoring high and came within 11.60 points of its widest margin. Jug (Lee284) scored 186.02, 9.14 above the previous best of 176.88, and beat Lucky Strike (drewkim), who scored 83.72, by 102.30, a margin exceeded only by the 113.90 of week 2. The week also held the third- and fourth-closest finishes of the season, 2.56 and 3.36 points. The six games totaled 1,466.52 points, the second-lowest week of the seven.
Jug's score in week 7, the highest of the 84 team scores this season. Every one of its ten starters scored 8 or more.
A 103.30-Point Spread Between the High and the Low

The week's scores ran from 186.02 to 82.72, a spread of 103.30 points. Six of the twelve teams scored 120 or more and four scored under 105: bigmoneyjos at 103.58, jiddyyyyyy at 100.60, drewkim at 83.72 and jjnhwg at 82.72. The last two are the sixth- and fifth-lowest scores of the season. The lowest is still edyun1's 62.98 in week 2.

Jug's 186.02 had no weak spot. Tony Pollard scored 36.5, Trey McBride 27.1, Quinshon Judkins 23.4, Javonte Williams 21.5 and Tre Tucker 21.3, and the two lowest of the ten starters, Tetairoa McMillan and kicker Jason Myers, scored 8 each. The best bench player, Tyler Allgeier, scored 7.9, so no one Lee284 left unused would have outscored a starter.

Neither low score is mainly a bench story. Bo Nix scored 26.28 on Lucky Strike's bench against C.J. Stroud's 16.52 at quarterback, a 9.76-point swap that would have put drewkim at 93.48, still 92.54 short of Jug. Two Finishes Inside Four Points

Two games ended 2.56 and 3.36 apart. Before this week the closest finishes of the season were 0.94 in week 4 and 1.78 in week 5, so week 7 now holds the third- and fourth-closest margins, ahead of the two 6.08 finishes in weeks 5 and 6.

The winner of the 2.56 game, edyun1, left 53.6 points on the bench, the most of any team in week 7, including Kirk Cousins's 20.4. The loser, asierbelay, left 11.3. In the 3.36 game, saiky7 left 36 and andychoe03 24.58, with Aaron Rodgers, a $1 claim, scoring 13.08 on the bench.
The results moved the standings in opposite directions. asierbelay's loss makes it 5-2 and saiky7's win makes it 5-2, so three teams, with Lee284, share the best record. andychoe03 is 3-4.
Four Teams at 4-3, and a Points Table Tighter Than the Standings

Points scored are closer than records. saiky7 leads the league with 988.92 points, tonypng has 988.62 at 4-3, Lee284 has 979.62 and asierbelay 978.04. The four are within 10.88 of each other, and the next team, nikhil1123, has 907.44, 70.60 behind asierbelay.
